Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. I'm copying Priyom and Laura from our infra & compliance teams to make sure nothing is missed. Summary answers below and I've attached a short matrix and runbook for onboarding private deployments.

Short answers (high level):
- Regions: Hosted (Redwood API) supports US (us-west-2 / us-east-1) and EU (eu-west-1) as standard. APAC (ap-northeast-1) is available via Dedicated/Private deployments on request. Customers can pin projects to a single region; we enforce region-level routing at the control plane and metadata layer.

- Private/Dedicated networking: We support two deployment models:
  * Dedicated VPC (our managed, single-tenant GPU pools) connected to your VPC via AWS Transit Gateway or VPC peering (customer preference).
  * Private edition (VPC-hosted control plane) where the entire inference layer is provisioned in your VPC/subnets. In both cases we can avoid public egress for inference traffic.

- Egress & endpoints:
  * Private endpoints: supported (Private ALB / NLB + interface endpoints) or Transit Gateway models; we do not require public Internet for model traffic in these modes.
  * Published IP ranges: for Dedicated pools we publish an authoritative CSV of outbound IP CIDRs per region (attached sample). For Private edition, traffic egress is under customer network controls.

- Audit logs & backups: Logs and audit trails for hosted API are stored in the same region as the dataset by default; backups are optional and can be configured to remain in-region. For Private deployments audit logs can be routed to your logging account (CloudWatch/ELK) via cross-account delivery.

- BYOK / KMS: We support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption-at-rest in Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API, we offer a customer-managed key option for enterprise accounts (requires KMS key grant and config).

Attachments included: redwood_vpc_network_matrix.pdf, runbook-vpc-onboarding.docx, public-ip-ranges-20261218.csv

Next steps: If you can confirm which model you prefer (Hosted with dedicated pool vs Private edition), Priyom can schedule a short 30-min network call and hand off detailed CIDR/IP ranges and peering steps.

Alex — good questions. Answers and attachments below; I've pasted the short answers first and attached a network diagram and updated IP ranges CSV for your team to attach to the SIG.

Answers: 
1) Dedicated pool IPs: the published CSV contains outbound NAT egress CIDRs per region (these are the IPs you will see when Redwood-originated traffic leaves the pool). Inbound is DNS-based to a private NLB (we recommend clients call our regional private endpoint DNS names). We include a stable CNAME per environment — no single static inbound IP is required for PrivateLink-style setups.

2) Transit Gateway vs PrivateLink: we support both. For low-latency, high-throughput customers we often recommend Transit Gateway peering with specific route table propagation. For strictly private, zero-public-surface setups we can use AWS PrivateLink/interface endpoints (we can provide interface endpoint service names during onboarding). Priyom — I'll follow up with the template route table and endpoint service name for Acme.

3) BYOK: yes — we support BYOK where the KMS key can live in the customer's account. For cross-account keys we require a KMS key policy that grants our service principal decrypt/encrypt usage; we provide a sample policy in the runbook.

Attached artifacts: network-diagram-acme.png (PNG), public-ip-ranges-20261220.csv (CSV), runbook-vpc-onboarding.docx (DOCX). I also included a one-page summary you can drop into the SIG evidence column.
